name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Iran claims tanker sank 15 Nov; US blockade
summary: Iran's IRGC says a supertanker sank after a mine strike near Hormuz on 15 Nov; claim unconfirmed; US blockade holds
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 15 Nov that two tankers on an unauthorised route in the southern Strait of Hormuz hit mines and a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude sank; there was no independent confirmation (AFP via RTÉ). UKMTO said it was aware of a report of a tanker attack in the Gulf with the crew safe (Gulf News). This follows the IRGC's claim to have downed a US drone over Qeshm on 14 Nov. Attacks on Gulf shipping and the restricted strait keep the Alert.
for_you: Follow FCDO travel advice for Iran and the Gulf states. Shipping and energy markets remain exposed to further disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.
rubric_hit: Alert: attacks on Gulf shipping and Hormuz restricted (mine strike claims 13–15 Nov)

sources.title: RTÉ (AFP) — Iran says supertanker carrying oil sinks in Hormuz Strait

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
